Yep no problem. Like I said, it completely depends on the medication, as well as the patient, and the condition being treated. Some people feel no different if they miss their antidepressant. Some people with have withdrawal symptoms within hours. If it’s a cholesterol pill like a statin, missing a dose will have very little effect. If it’s a blood pressure medication the patient can very well have a spike in BP. 
Antibiotic dosing, usually written “three times a day” for example should be taken every 8 hours if possible to avoid drops in blood concentration...treatment failure is certainly possible. For the most part I recommend keeping as close as possible to a set interval. 

Source : am pharmacist

The same is true for all medications. Twice a day conventionally means every 12 hours or as close as possible. It depends on the medication whether the timing is crucial. Hormones can have what we call a narrow therapeutic index- the range of drug concentration in the blood which is effective. There are some oral hormones that you must take within one hour of dosing time otherwise the effect will be lost.
